intro.title: Exodus 1 · chapter outline
intro.note: This native text diagram separates the chapter into source-based reading stages. Events, instructions, songs, laws, and summaries follow the text; the cards do not claim to depict one place or moment.

hotspots.title: Israel grows; Joseph’s generation dies
hotspots.note: Timing: Verses 1–5 name the households and count the people; verses 6–7 summarize deaths and later growth.
hotspots.diagram_note: Jacob’s sons enter Egypt with their households; Joseph and his generation die, and Israel multiplies.

hotspots.title: A new king fears Israel’s growth
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech. Separates the king’s stated motive from later labor effects.
hotspots.diagram_note: A new king fears Israel’s growth and proposes measures to keep them from joining Egypt’s enemies.

hotspots.title: Taskmasters build Pithom and Raamses
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event. Retains Pithom and Raamses as text names without drawing a modern map.
hotspots.diagram_note: Taskmasters set over Israel force them to build Pharaoh’s store cities, Pithom and Raamses.

hotspots.title: Affliction increases, but Israel multiplies
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated summary. Shows the stated contrast between hard service and continued growth.
hotspots.diagram_note: Shows the stated contrast between hard service and continued growth.

hotspots.title: Shiphrah and Puah refuse the king’s command
hotspots.note: Timing: The king’s order, the midwives’ refusal, the exchange, and the outcome are distinct narrated steps.
hotspots.diagram_note: Midwives refuse the order; the king questions them.

hotspots.title: Pharaoh orders Hebrew sons cast into the Nile
hotspots.note: Timing: instruction / decree. Makes the decree and its stated distinction between sons and daughters visible without depicting harm to infants.
hotspots.diagram_note: Pharaoh orders every son born to the Hebrews cast into the river, while every daughter is to live.

intro.title: Exodus 2 · chapter outline
intro.note: This native text diagram separates the chapter into source-based reading stages. Events, instructions, songs, laws, and summaries follow the text; the cards do not claim to depict one place or moment.

hotspots.title: A son is born and hidden for three months
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event and time summary. Captures the birth and concealment interval without inventing names or appearance.
hotspots.diagram_note: Captures the birth and concealment interval without inventing names or appearance.

hotspots.title: Basket found; Pharaoh’s daughter shows compassion
hotspots.note: Timing: The basket is placed in verse 3; the sister watches in verse 4; discovery and compassion follow in verses 5–6.
hotspots.diagram_note: Pharaoh’s daughter finds the basket and pities the weeping child; his sister watches.

hotspots.title: The sister offers to call a Hebrew nurse
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech. Preserves the sister’s proposal and Pharaoh’s daughter’s answer as reported dialogue.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses’s sister offers to call a Hebrew nurse, and Pharaoh’s daughter tells her to go.

hotspots.title: The child’s mother nurses him for wages
hotspots.note: Timing: instruction and narrated action. Marks the text’s stated arrangement without supplying an unnamed mother’s portrait.
hotspots.diagram_note: Pharaoh’s daughter pays the child’s mother to nurse him.

hotspots.title: The child is brought back and named Moses
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event and naming. Records the naming explanation at its actual point in the story.
hotspots.diagram_note: The child is brought to Pharaoh’s daughter, who names him Moses, saying she drew him from the water.

hotspots.title: Moses sees an Egyptian striking a Hebrew
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event. Anchors the conflict in the stated verse without identifying either unnamed man.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses sees an Egyptian striking a Hebrew, one of his brethren.

hotspots.title: Moses kills the Egyptian and hides him in the sand
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event. Keeps the text’s event in a restrained textual node; no graphic depiction.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses looks around, kills the Egyptian, and hides him in the sand.

hotspots.title: A Hebrew challenges Moses the next day
hotspots.note: Timing: reported dialogue. Shows the second conflict and the quoted challenge separately from the earlier act.
hotspots.diagram_note: Next day Moses rebukes two fighting Hebrews; one challenges him over the Egyptian’s death.

hotspots.title: Moses flees Pharaoh and sits by a well in Midian
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event. Marks the narrated change of place without adding route geography.
hotspots.diagram_note: When Pharaoh seeks to kill him, Moses flees to Midian and sits by a well.

hotspots.title: Moses helps the seven daughters at the well
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event. Links the named number and the act of assistance to the well episode.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses helps seven daughters water their flock after shepherds drive them away.

hotspots.title: Reuel welcomes Moses to eat bread
hotspots.note: Timing: reported dialogue. Keeps the daughters’ report and their father’s response in sequence.
hotspots.diagram_note: Reuel asks his daughters why they left the Egyptian who helped them, then invites him to eat.

hotspots.title: Zipporah is given to Moses; Gershom is born
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated summary. Records marriage and the named son without adding portrait details.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses stays with Reuel, marries Zipporah, and names his son Gershom.

hotspots.title: Israel sighs and cries because of bondage
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event. Names the people’s reported distress before the response verbs.
hotspots.diagram_note: After Egypt’s king dies, Israel groans under bondage and cries out to God.

hotspots.title: God hears and remembers the covenant
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated statement. Preserves the text’s stated verbs and named patriarchs without adding an explanation.
hotspots.diagram_note: God hears Israel’s groaning and remembers his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

hotspots.title: God looks upon Israel and has respect unto them
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated statement. Closes the chapter’s response chain at the exact verse.
hotspots.diagram_note: God looks upon the children of Israel and acknowledges them.

intro.title: Exodus 3 · chapter outline
intro.note: This native text diagram separates the chapter into source-based reading stages. Events, instructions, songs, laws, and summaries follow the text; the cards do not claim to depict one place or moment.

hotspots.title: Moses leads the flock to Horeb
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated setting. Retains the verse’s named place without asserting a modern site or mapped route.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses leads Jethro’s flock to Horeb, the mountain of God.

hotspots.title: The bush burns; Moses hides his face
hotspots.note: Timing: The bush, call, shoe instruction, identity statement, and Moses’s response are linked to verses 2–6.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD calls Moses from a burning bush, tells him to remove his shoes, and Moses hides his face.

hotspots.title: The LORD sees and hears Israel’s sorrow
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech. Gathers the explicit verbs while keeping them as reported speech.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD says he has seen Israel’s affliction, heard their cry, and knows their sorrows.

hotspots.title: The LORD promises a good land
hotspots.note: Timing: promise / prediction. Marks a future promise and the named peoples in the source without a map.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD promises to bring Israel from Egypt to a good land flowing with milk and honey.

hotspots.title: Moses is sent to Pharaoh
hotspots.note: Timing: instruction / commission. Separates the commission from its future outcome.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD sends Moses to Pharaoh to bring the children of Israel out of Egypt.

hotspots.title: Moses asks who he is; God promises help
hotspots.note: Timing: reported dialogue and promise. Captures the question, answer, and promised sign at the mountain.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses asks how he can lead Israel; the LORD promises to be with him and gives a sign at Horeb.

hotspots.title: Moses asks what name he should give Israel
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech. Marks the question that frames the answer.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses asks what name he should give if Israel asks who sent him.

hotspots.title: “I AM THAT I AM” is given as the message
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech. Uses the source wording as a quoted response, clearly separated from explanation.
hotspots.diagram_note: Uses the source wording as a quoted response, clearly separated from explanation.

hotspots.title: The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech. Preserves the repeated names and memorial statement.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD names the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as his memorial forever.

hotspots.title: Israel’s elders hear the LORD’s message
hotspots.note: Timing: instruction and reported speech. Separates the instruction to the elders from the future journey.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses tells Israel’s elders the LORD has seen their affliction and will bring them to Canaan.

hotspots.title: Ask Pharaoh for three days’ journey to sacrifice
hotspots.note: Timing: planned request. Shows the requested leave as speech, not a route map.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses and Israel’s elders are to ask Pharaoh for three days to sacrifice in the wilderness.

hotspots.title: Pharaoh’s refusal and later release are foretold
hotspots.note: Timing: prediction. Keeps prediction distinct from later narrated events.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD says Egypt’s king will not let Israel go, then foretells striking Egypt with wonders.

hotspots.title: Israel will leave with Egypt’s goods
hotspots.note: Timing: prediction. Records the stated expectation without illustrating a later transaction as present.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD promises favor; Israel’s women will ask Egyptians for silver, gold, and clothing.

intro.title: Exodus 4 · chapter outline
intro.note: This native text diagram separates the chapter into source-based reading stages. Events, instructions, songs, laws, and summaries follow the text; the cards do not claim to depict one place or moment.

hotspots.title: Moses fears Israel will not believe
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech. Makes the question that prompts the signs visible without implying the signs already occurred.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses fears the Israelites will not believe or listen to him.

hotspots.title: The rod becomes a serpent and returns to a rod
hotspots.note: Timing: All three current nodes are active on verses 2–4 and keep the states in order.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses casts down the rod; it becomes a serpent, and he takes its tail so it becomes a rod again.

hotspots.title: The first sign is given so Israel may believe
hotspots.note: Timing: explanation of sign. States the sign’s stated purpose without duplicating its pictured states.
hotspots.diagram_note: The sign is given so Israel may believe that the LORD, God of their fathers, appeared to Moses.

hotspots.title: Moses’s hand is made leprous, then restored
hotspots.note: Timing: instruction followed by narrated event. Keeps the two successive states distinct; do not add clinical detail.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses’s hand turns leprous as snow, then is restored when he puts it in his bosom again.

hotspots.title: River water will become blood on dry land
hotspots.note: Timing: conditional prediction. Labels the third sign as conditional forecast; it is not the later river plague event.
hotspots.diagram_note: If Israel rejects the first two signs, Moses is to pour river water on dry land, where it will become blood.

hotspots.title: Moses says he is slow of speech
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech. Anchors the stated objection.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses tells the LORD he is not eloquent and is slow of speech and tongue.

hotspots.title: The LORD promises to be with Moses’s mouth
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech and instruction. Keeps the answer and instruction in their own verses.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD promises to be with Moses’s mouth and teach him what to say.

hotspots.title: Aaron will speak for Moses
hotspots.note: Timing: reported instruction. Shows the stated speaking relationship without assigning a historical portrait.
hotspots.diagram_note: Aaron will speak for Moses; Moses is to tell him the LORD’s words, and the LORD will teach them what to do.

hotspots.title: Moses is told to take the rod for signs
hotspots.note: Timing: instruction. Records the instruction at the end of the exchange.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses is told to take the rod with which he will perform signs.

hotspots.title: Moses asks Jethro to return to his brethren
hotspots.note: Timing: reported dialogue. Captures the request and permission without adding travel details.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses asks Jethro to let him return to his brethren in Egypt; Jethro tells him to go in peace.

hotspots.title: Moses returns toward Egypt with family and rod
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event. Marks the narrated departure and the stated objects/persons.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses returns toward Egypt with his family and the rod after the LORD says his enemies are dead.

hotspots.title: Wonders foretold; Pharaoh’s heart will harden
hotspots.note: Timing: instruction and prediction. Keeps the forecast distinct from the signs that follow.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD tells Moses to perform wonders before Pharaoh and says his heart will harden.

hotspots.title: Israel as firstborn; Egypt’s firstborn warned
hotspots.note: Timing: reported instruction and prediction. Preserves the wording as a warning, not as the midnight event.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses calls Israel the LORD’s firstborn and warns Pharaoh his firstborn will die if he refuses.

hotspots.title: Zipporah circumcises her son
hotspots.note: Verses 24–26 leave the referents of “him” and “his feet” ambiguous; preserve the narrated order without resolving them.
hotspots.diagram_note: Zipporah circumcises her son at the lodging place; the text says, “he let him go.”

hotspots.title: Aaron meets Moses at the mountain of God
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event. Marks the meeting in the verse’s stated place.
hotspots.diagram_note: Aaron meets Moses at the mountain of God and kisses him.

hotspots.title: Moses tells Aaron the LORD’s words and signs
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech. Separates their conversation from the later elders’ gathering.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses tells Aaron all the LORD’s words and the signs he commanded him.

hotspots.title: Moses and Aaron gather Israel’s elders
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event and reported speech. Shows the gathering and Aaron’s report/signs as the next steps.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses and Aaron gather the elders; Aaron reports the LORD’s words and performs signs.

hotspots.title: The people believe and worship
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated response. Closes the response sequence at the actual reported outcome.
hotspots.diagram_note: The people believe when they hear the LORD has seen their affliction, then bow their heads and worship.

intro.title: Exodus 5 · chapter outline
intro.note: This native text diagram separates the chapter into source-based reading stages. Events, instructions, songs, laws, and summaries follow the text; the cards do not claim to depict one place or moment.

hotspots.title: Moses asks for release; Pharaoh refuses
hotspots.note: Timing: The three-days’ request and Pharaoh’s response are speech; no divine or royal portrait is required.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses and Aaron ask Pharaoh to let Israel worship; Pharaoh refuses and says they have too much rest.

hotspots.title: Taskmasters are commanded to withhold straw
hotspots.note: Timing: instruction / decree. Marks the source of the new requirement.
hotspots.diagram_note: Pharaoh orders the taskmasters and officers to stop giving Israel straw for making bricks.

hotspots.title: The same brick tally is demanded
hotspots.note: Timing: instruction / decree. Shows the unchanged quota and stated accusation without inventing numbers.
hotspots.diagram_note: Pharaoh keeps the same brick quota and calls the people idle for asking to worship.

hotspots.title: Stubble gathering under unchanged quotas
hotspots.note: Verses 10–11 deliver Pharaoh’s order; verses 12–13 report Israel gathering stubble and taskmasters demanding the usual daily work.
hotspots.diagram_note: Israel gathers stubble while taskmasters still demand the daily brick tally.

hotspots.title: Israelite officers are beaten over the brick tally
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event and reported question. Identifies the consequence of the unchanged quota without a violent scene.
hotspots.diagram_note: Israelite officers are beaten for the missing brick tally and questioned by taskmasters.

hotspots.title: Officers question Pharaoh’s treatment
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech. Keeps the appeal in the officers’ own words.
hotspots.diagram_note: The officers tell Pharaoh they get no straw yet must make bricks and are beaten.

hotspots.title: Pharaoh calls them idle and orders the same work
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech and instruction. Shows the answer and renewed demand without generalizing beyond the passage.
hotspots.diagram_note: Pharaoh calls the people idle and orders them to gather straw while making the same number of bricks.

hotspots.title: The officers see their case is worsened
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated response. Marks the narrated realization after Pharaoh’s order.
hotspots.diagram_note: The officers see their case is worsened when Pharaoh refuses to reduce the daily brick tally.

hotspots.title: The officers meet Moses and Aaron
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event. Anchors the encounter in the verse.
hotspots.diagram_note: The officers meet Moses and Aaron as they leave Pharaoh.

hotspots.title: They say Pharaoh now has a sword against them
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech. Records the accusation as speech, without depicting a literal sword.
hotspots.diagram_note: The officers accuse Moses and Aaron of giving Pharaoh cause to kill them.

hotspots.title: Moses questions the worsening suffering
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech and lament. Preserves the chapter-ending question and the reported worsening as the final state.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses asks why Pharaoh increased Israel’s burden instead of delivering them.

intro.title: Exodus 6 · chapter outline
intro.note: This native text diagram separates the chapter into source-based reading stages. Events, instructions, songs, laws, and summaries follow the text; the cards do not claim to depict one place or moment.

hotspots.title: Pharaoh will release Israel
hotspots.note: Timing: prediction. Marks the opening answer as a forecast.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD says Pharaoh will let Israel go by a strong hand and drive them out of Egypt.

hotspots.title: The LORD names himself and recalls the covenant
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech and retrospective statement. Links the names and covenant statement without imposing chronology beyond the verses.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD names himself Jehovah, recalls his covenant, and hears Israel’s groaning.

hotspots.title: Israel will be brought out and redeemed
hotspots.note: Timing: promise. Keeps the promises grouped in the source’s sequence.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD promises to bring Israel out of Egypt, redeem them, and take them as his people.

hotspots.title: The LORD promises an inheritance in the land
hotspots.note: Timing: promise. Marks the final promise as future.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD promises to bring Israel into the land sworn to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and give it to them.

hotspots.title: Israel does not hear because of anguish
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated response. Preserves the stated reason instead of implying disbelief without cause.
hotspots.diagram_note: Israel does not heed Moses because of anguish of spirit and cruel bondage.

hotspots.title: The LORD tells Moses to speak to Pharaoh
hotspots.note: Timing: instruction. Marks the instruction and its intended audience.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD tells Moses to speak to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and demand that he send Israel out.

hotspots.title: Moses cites Israel’s silence and his speech
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech. Keeps Moses’s objection as reported speech.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses says Israel has not heeded him and asks how Pharaoh will hear his uncircumcised lips.

hotspots.title: Moses and Aaron are charged to bring Israel out
hotspots.note: Timing: instruction / commission. Records the assigned task as a commission, not its result.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD charges Moses and Aaron to bring Israel out of Egypt.

hotspots.title: Reuben, Simeon, and Levi genealogy
hotspots.note: Verses 14–25 list descendants of Reuben, Simeon, and Levi and identify the line that includes Aaron and Moses.
hotspots.diagram_note: The genealogy lists Reuben’s, Simeon’s, and Levi’s houses and names Aaron and Moses.

hotspots.title: Moses and Aaron charged to bring Israel out
hotspots.note: Timing: retrospective summary. Marks the chapter’s recap and named agents.
hotspots.diagram_note: This is the Moses and Aaron whom the LORD commanded to bring Israel out of Egypt.

hotspots.title: Moses is again commanded to speak
hotspots.note: Timing: reported instruction. Shows the repeated commission, not a new speech event with additional content.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD again tells Moses to speak all his words to Pharaoh.

hotspots.title: Moses again says Pharaoh will not hear him
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech. Closes the chapter with his stated concern.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses again says Pharaoh will not hear him because he is of uncircumcised lips.

intro.title: Exodus 7 · chapter outline
intro.note: This native text diagram separates the chapter into source-based reading stages. Events, instructions, songs, laws, and summaries follow the text; the cards do not claim to depict one place or moment.

hotspots.title: Moses speaks and Aaron is his prophet to Pharaoh
hotspots.note: Timing: instruction. Clarifies the role relationship as stated, without interpreting “god to Pharaoh” as a portrait.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD makes Moses as God to Pharaoh and appoints Aaron as his prophet.

hotspots.title: Refusal and signs are foretold
hotspots.note: Timing: prediction. Keeps the predicted refusal and purpose of signs separate from later events.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD foretells Pharaoh’s refusal and many signs, so Egypt will know that he is the LORD.

hotspots.title: Moses and Aaron obey; their ages are stated
hotspots.note: Timing: retrospective summary. Records the chapter’s summary and explicit ages without inferring their appearance.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses and Aaron obey; Moses is eighty and Aaron eighty-three when they speak to Pharaoh.

hotspots.title: Rod sign; magicians imitate; Pharaoh refuses
hotspots.note: Verses 8–9 set the sign before Pharaoh; verse 10 records Aaron’s rod becoming a serpent, verses 11–12 the magicians’ imitation and its defeat, and verse 13 Pharaoh’s hardened heart.
hotspots.diagram_note: Aaron’s rod becomes a serpent; magicians imitate, but it swallows their rods and Pharaoh refuses.

hotspots.title: Pharaoh refuses to let the people go
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech / announcement. Sets the stated cause and the message delivered at the river.
hotspots.diagram_note: Pharaoh’s heart is hardened; Moses is told to meet him by the river with the rod.

hotspots.title: The LORD says the river will be turned to blood
hotspots.note: Timing: prediction. Keeps the sign forecast and effects in future language.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD foretells that the river will become blood and its fish will die.

hotspots.title: Water turns to blood; fish die
hotspots.note: Verse 19 commands Aaron to stretch his rod over Egypt’s waters; verses 20–21 report the river turning to blood and its fish dying.
hotspots.diagram_note: Aaron strikes the river with his rod; the water becomes blood, and the fish die.

hotspots.title: Magicians imitate; Pharaoh will not hear
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event and response. Separates imitation and refusal from the initial plague event.
hotspots.diagram_note: The magicians imitate the sign, but Pharaoh’s heart remains hardened and he does not heed them.

hotspots.title: Egyptians dig beside the river for water
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event. Records the stated response without inventing wells or locations.
hotspots.diagram_note: Egyptians dig along the river for drinking water because they cannot drink the river water.

hotspots.title: Seven days after the river is struck
hotspots.note: Timing: time summary. Keeps the text’s duration statement exact; no inferred calendar dates.
hotspots.diagram_note: Seven days pass after the LORD strikes the river.

intro.title: Exodus 8 · chapter outline
intro.note: This native text diagram separates the chapter into source-based reading stages. Events, instructions, songs, laws, and summaries follow the text; the cards do not claim to depict one place or moment.

hotspots.title: Frogs are announced and cover Egypt
hotspots.note: Verses 1–4 announce frogs entering homes and vessels; verses 5–6 report Aaron stretching out his rod and frogs covering Egypt.
hotspots.diagram_note: Frogs are announced; Aaron’s rod brings them across Egypt, into houses and kneading troughs.

hotspots.title: Magicians bring frogs; Pharaoh asks relief
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event and reported speech. Shows the imitation and request as two consecutive actions.
hotspots.diagram_note: The magicians bring up frogs, and Pharaoh calls Moses and Aaron to ask the LORD for relief.

hotspots.title: Pharaoh appoints tomorrow for the frogs to depart
hotspots.note: Timing: reported dialogue and prediction. Keeps the stated time and predicted relief in the dialogue.
hotspots.diagram_note: Pharaoh asks Moses to appoint when the frogs should leave; Moses says it will be tomorrow.

hotspots.title: Moses cries unto the LORD because of the frogs
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event. Marks the prayer before its reported outcome.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses cries to the LORD about the frogs, as Pharaoh had asked.

hotspots.title: Frogs die and are gathered in heaps
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated outcome. Makes the narrated consequence visible without graphic detail.
hotspots.diagram_note: The frogs die in houses, villages, and fields, and the people gather them in heaps.

hotspots.title: Pharaoh hardens his heart after respite
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated response. Closes the unit with the stated response.
hotspots.diagram_note: When Pharaoh sees relief, he hardens his heart and refuses to listen.

hotspots.title: Dust becomes lice; magicians fail
hotspots.note: Verse 16 gives the command; verses 17–18 report lice and the magicians’ failure, and verse 19 records their words to Pharaoh.
hotspots.diagram_note: At the LORD’s command Aaron strikes the dust, which becomes lice; the magicians cannot reproduce the sign.

hotspots.title: Swarms enter Egypt; Goshen is set apart
hotspots.note: Verses 20–21 announce the swarms; verses 22–23 foretell Goshen’s distinction, and verse 24 reports the swarm entering Egypt’s houses and land.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD announces a division between Goshen and Egypt; swarms come into Egypt’s houses and land.

hotspots.title: Pharaoh bargains; swarms depart; refusal resumes
hotspots.note: Timing: Keep Pharaoh’s proposed limits, Moses’s reply, prayer, removal of flies, and final refusal in order.
hotspots.diagram_note: Pharaoh offers limits on sacrifice; Moses prays, the LORD removes the flies, and Pharaoh refuses again.

scenes.title: Exodus 9 chapter outline
scenes.caption: Editorial chapter diagram · events and instructions are separate reading stages, not one scene

art.alt: Editorial chapter diagram for Exodus 9: 11 source-based cards partition the chapter into reading stages. This is not a geographical map or a single scene.

intro.title: Exodus 9 · chapter outline
intro.note: This native text diagram separates the chapter into source-based reading stages. Events, instructions, songs, laws, and summaries follow the text; the cards do not claim to depict one place or moment.

hotspots.title: Livestock plague; Israel’s cattle are spared
hotspots.note: Verses 1–5 warn of the disease and appoint the next day; verse 6 reports the deaths and verse 7 Pharaoh’s inspection and refusal.
hotspots.diagram_note: A livestock plague is announced; Egyptian cattle die, Israel’s live, and Pharaoh refuses.

hotspots.title: Moses and Aaron scatter furnace ashes
hotspots.note: Timing: instruction then narrated event. Separates the instruction from its narrated action.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses scatters furnace ashes; boils break out on people and animals across Egypt.

hotspots.title: The magicians cannot stand before Moses
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated condition and response. Records the stated effect without graphic or diagnostic detail.
hotspots.diagram_note: The magicians cannot stand before Moses because of the boils, and Pharaoh does not heed the LORD’s word.

hotspots.title: The hail is announced for the next day
hotspots.note: Timing: announcement / prediction. Keeps the predicted event in the future and includes the stated warning.
hotspots.diagram_note: Hail is announced for tomorrow; Pharaoh is told to shelter people and cattle from the field.

hotspots.title: Some servants shelter people and cattle
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated response. Shows one response to the warning.
hotspots.diagram_note: Pharaoh’s servants who fear the LORD’s word bring their servants and cattle into the houses.

hotspots.title: Others leave people and cattle outside
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated response. Contrasts the second response without inventing specific people.
hotspots.diagram_note: Those who do not regard the LORD’s word leave their servants and cattle in the field.

hotspots.title: Hail and fire in Egypt; Goshen has no hail
hotspots.note: Verse 22 commands hail; verses 23–25 report the storm and damage; verse 26 says there is no hail in Goshen.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD sends hail and fire across Egypt; Goshen, where Israel lives, has no hail.

hotspots.title: Pharaoh confesses and asks for relief
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech. Shows the confession and request as speech, not as repentance beyond the words.
hotspots.diagram_note: Pharaoh says he has sinned, calls the LORD righteous, and asks Moses to entreat him so the hail will cease.

hotspots.title: Hail destroys barley and flax, not wheat
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated report. Preserves the crop distinction and source wording without substituting modern crop states.
hotspots.diagram_note: Hail strikes the barley and flax, while wheat and rye are not yet grown and remain unstruck.

hotspots.title: Moses spreads his hands; thunder and hail cease
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event and outcome. Marks the narrated prayer and cessation after the report.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses spreads his hands to the LORD; thunder, hail, and rain cease.

hotspots.title: Pharaoh and his servants harden their hearts again
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated response. Closes with the stated reversal.
hotspots.diagram_note: After the storm ceases, Pharaoh and his servants harden their hearts and refuse to release Israel.

intro.title: Exodus 10 · chapter outline
intro.note: This native text diagram separates the chapter into source-based reading stages. Events, instructions, songs, laws, and summaries follow the text; the cards do not claim to depict one place or moment.

hotspots.title: The signs are to be told to later generations
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech / purpose. Shows the passage’s stated purpose for remembrance.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses recounts Egypt’s signs to his children and grandchildren so they may know the LORD.

hotspots.title: Locusts are announced if Pharaoh refuses
hotspots.note: Timing: announcement / prediction. Keeps the threat and forecast in the future.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD warns that locusts will cover Egypt and consume what the hail left if Pharaoh refuses again.

hotspots.title: Pharaoh’s servants urge him to let the people go
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech. Marks the reported counsel before the negotiation.
hotspots.diagram_note: Pharaoh’s servants urge him to release the people to serve the LORD, saying Egypt is destroyed.

hotspots.title: Pharaoh asks who may go, then limits them
hotspots.note: Timing: reported dialogue and instruction. Makes the negotiating limit explicit and distinct from the actual departure.
hotspots.diagram_note: Pharaoh limits release to men; Moses says all Israel and their flocks must go.

hotspots.title: Locusts cover Egypt and consume what hail left
hotspots.note: Verse 12 commands locusts; verse 13 reports the east wind and their arrival, and verses 14–15 their spread and consumption.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD commands locusts; an east wind brings them, and they cover Egypt and consume what the hail left.

hotspots.title: Pharaoh confesses and asks Moses to forgive him
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech. Records the words without inferring lasting repentance.
hotspots.diagram_note: Pharaoh confesses his sin and asks Moses to forgive him and entreat the LORD to remove this death.

hotspots.title: Moses entreats the LORD
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event. Keeps the prayer before the response.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses leaves Pharaoh and entreats the LORD.

hotspots.title: A west wind carries the locusts into the Red sea
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event. Uses the named destination as text, not a plotted route.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD sends a strong west wind that carries every locust into the Red Sea.

hotspots.title: Pharaoh’s heart is hardened again
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated response. Closes the response sequence.
hotspots.diagram_note: After the locusts depart, the LORD hardens Pharaoh’s heart and he refuses to let Israel go.

hotspots.title: Darkness in Egypt; Israel has light
hotspots.note: Verse 21 announces darkness; verses 22–23 report its three-day duration and Israel’s light.
hotspots.diagram_note: Darkness covers Egypt three days, while all the children of Israel have light in their dwellings.

hotspots.title: Pharaoh offers release but keeps livestock
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech. Shows the proposed restriction.
hotspots.diagram_note: Pharaoh offers release but commands Israel to leave its flocks and herds behind.

hotspots.title: Moses says the cattle must go for sacrifice
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech. Captures the stated reason and refusal of the restriction.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses says Israel’s cattle must go because they do not know which animals they will use to serve the LORD.

hotspots.title: Pharaoh forbids Moses to see him again
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech. Shows the final command and Moses’s reply as dialogue.
hotspots.diagram_note: Pharaoh orders Moses never to see him again; Moses agrees they will not meet again.

hotspots.title: One more plague; Israel asks for Egypt’s goods
hotspots.note: Timing: The coming plague and asking for goods are prospective instructions; verse 3 reports favor and Moses’s standing.
hotspots.diagram_note: One final plague will make Pharaoh drive Israel out; they are told to ask for silver and gold.

hotspots.title: Firstborn death is announced for midnight
hotspots.note: Timing: announcement / prediction. Keeps the death and great cry as prediction; do not depict fulfillment.
hotspots.diagram_note: At midnight Egypt’s human and animal firstborn will die, bringing a great cry.

hotspots.title: Moses announces a distinction for Israel
hotspots.note: Timing: announcement / prediction. Keeps the promised distinction prospective.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD distinguishes Israel from Egypt; no dog will move its tongue against them.

hotspots.title: Servants will plead for release; Pharaoh refuses
hotspots.note: Timing: Verse 8 predicts a future plea and reports Moses’s exit; verses 9–10 summarize refusal and wonders.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses predicts Pharaoh’s servants will plead for Israel to leave; refusal and wonders will follow.

intro.title: Exodus 12 · chapter outline
intro.note: This native text diagram separates the chapter into source-based reading stages. Events, instructions, songs, laws, and summaries follow the text; the cards do not claim to depict one place or moment.

hotspots.title: This month is to be the beginning of months
hotspots.note: Timing: instruction. Preserves the instruction without inferring a modern calendar date.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD declares this month the first of the year for Israel.

hotspots.title: Passover meal and blood sign; judgment announced
hotspots.note: Verses 3–11 command household preparation; verses 12–13 announce judgment and explain the sign. Blood application is instructed, not narrated as already performed.
hotspots.diagram_note: Households prepare the Passover lamb; judgment is announced and blood named as a sign.

hotspots.title: Keep the memorial feast through the generations
hotspots.note: Timing: instruction. Separates the ordinance from the later historical departure.
hotspots.diagram_note: Israel is commanded to keep the Passover memorial feast through its generations.

hotspots.title: Remove leaven and keep the seven-day feast
hotspots.note: Timing: instruction. Shows duration and household instruction without adding ritual detail.
hotspots.diagram_note: Israel is to remove leaven and eat unleavened bread for seven days.

hotspots.title: Moses instructs elders to kill a lamb
hotspots.note: Timing: instruction. Marks the addressed instruction.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses tells Israel’s elders to take a lamb according to their families and kill the Passover.

hotspots.title: Hyssop, blood, and staying indoors until dawn
hotspots.note: Timing: instruction. Keeps the action in imperative language and avoids a painting that implies execution.
hotspots.diagram_note: Use hyssop to mark the doorposts with blood; stay inside until morning.

hotspots.title: The LORD says he will pass over the marked door
hotspots.note: Timing: prediction. Labels the promised action as future relative to the instruction.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD says he will pass through Egypt but pass over the blood-marked doors and spare those houses.

hotspots.title: Passover ordinance; children learn its meaning
hotspots.note: Timing: The children’s question is future; verse 27 reports the explanation and the people’s bowing and worship.
hotspots.diagram_note: Israel explains the LORD’s Passover to children; the people bow and worship.

hotspots.title: Israel does as the LORD commanded
hotspots.note: Timing: retrospective summary. Retains the summary without claiming details the verse does not specify.
hotspots.diagram_note: Israel does as the LORD commanded Moses and Aaron.

hotspots.title: The firstborn die at midnight
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event. Records the event without depicting dead children or graphic harm.
hotspots.diagram_note: At midnight the LORD strikes Egypt’s firstborn, from Pharaoh’s household to the captive and the cattle.

hotspots.title: A great cry; Pharaoh orders Israel to leave
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event and reported speech. Shows the reported aftermath and release command as ordered steps.
hotspots.diagram_note: Egypt cries after the deaths; Pharaoh orders Israel to leave with flocks and herds.

hotspots.title: Egyptians urge the people to depart in haste
hotspots.note: Timing: reported speech / response. Marks the public urgency that precedes the journey.
hotspots.diagram_note: The Egyptians urge Israel to leave quickly, fearing they will all die.

hotspots.title: Unleavened dough is carried in kneadingtroughs
hotspots.note: Verse 34 says the people take their unrisen dough and carry the kneadingtroughs in their clothes on their shoulders.
hotspots.diagram_note: Israel carries unrisen dough in kneadingtroughs wrapped in clothing on their shoulders.

hotspots.title: Israel receives silver, gold, and raiment
hotspots.note: Verses 35–36 report Israel asking for silver, gold, and raiment, and the LORD giving them favor with the Egyptians.
hotspots.diagram_note: Israel receives silver, gold, and clothing from the Egyptians, who grant what the people ask.

hotspots.title: Israel journeys from Rameses to Succoth
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event. Uses only the two text-named places; no mapped route or modern identifications.
hotspots.diagram_note: Israel journeys from Rameses to Succoth; about six hundred thousand men on foot go, besides children.

hotspots.title: A mixed multitude and flocks go up with Israel
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event. Identifies the stated company without an exact visual count.
hotspots.diagram_note: A mixed multitude goes up with Israel, along with flocks, herds, and much cattle.

hotspots.title: Unleavened cakes are baked from the dough
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated event. Keeps baking as a later result, separate from carrying the dough.
hotspots.diagram_note: Israel bakes unleavened cakes from the dough carried out of Egypt.

hotspots.title: The sojourning in Egypt is stated as 430 years
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated time statement. Preserves the stated span and selfsame-day wording without a timeline imported from elsewhere.
hotspots.diagram_note: The sojourn in Egypt is 430 years; Israel leaves on that selfsame day.

hotspots.title: Passover night kept through generations
hotspots.note: Timing: instruction / remembrance. Shows the remembrance statement separately from the departure scene.
hotspots.diagram_note: The Passover night is to be observed unto the LORD by Israel through its generations.

hotspots.title: Passover eligibility and household rules
hotspots.note: Timing: instruction / ordinance. Organizes the stated eligibility conditions without adding later legal interpretation.
hotspots.diagram_note: Circumcised servants and resident strangers may eat Passover; foreign and hired servants may not.

hotspots.title: One law for homeborn and foreigner
hotspots.note: Timing: instruction / ordinance. Keeps the concluding rule attached to its exact source.
hotspots.diagram_note: One law applies to the homeborn and the stranger who sojourns among Israel.

hotspots.title: Israel does as the LORD commanded
hotspots.note: Timing: retrospective summary. Marks the obedience summary.
hotspots.diagram_note: All Israel does as the LORD commanded Moses and Aaron.

hotspots.title: The LORD brings Israel out that day
hotspots.note: Timing: narrated summary. Closes the chapter with the text’s stated outcome, without adding geography.
hotspots.diagram_note: On that selfsame day the LORD brings Israel’s hosts out of Egypt.

intro.title: Exodus 13 · chapter outline
intro.note: This native text diagram separates the chapter into source-based reading stages. Events, instructions, songs, laws, and summaries follow the text; the cards do not claim to depict one place or moment.

hotspots.title: Firstborn dedicated to the LORD
hotspots.note: Stage type: instruction. The LORD claims Israel's firstborn, human and animal, as holy to him. Introduces the chapter's firstborn theme before its later redemption rules.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD claims Israel's firstborn, human and animal, as holy to him.

hotspots.title: Unleavened bread recalls deliverance
hotspots.note: Stage type: instruction and memorial. Keep the unleavened-bread feast, and explain to the next generation that the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt. Connects an annual observance with remembered deliverance and teaching children.
hotspots.diagram_note: Israel keeps the unleavened-bread feast and teaches that the LORD brought them from Egypt.

hotspots.title: Firstborn redemption rules
hotspots.note: Stage type: instruction. Set apart firstborn males; redeem a firstling ass with a lamb and redeem human firstborn. Separates the concrete firstborn rules from the later explanation to a child.
hotspots.diagram_note: Set apart firstborn males; redeem a firstling ass with a lamb and redeem human firstborn.

hotspots.title: A child asks why
hotspots.note: Stage type: question and explanation. When a child asks about the practice, answer that the LORD brought Israel out with strength; the firstborn sign recalls that deliverance. Makes the question-and-answer teaching pattern visible without blending it into the rule.
hotspots.diagram_note: A child asks about the firstborn practice; the answer recalls the LORD’s deliverance.

hotspots.title: Departure guided by cloud and fire
hotspots.note: Stage type: narrative action and guidance. God leads the people away from the Philistine road; Moses carries Joseph's bones, and the cloud and fire pillars guide them. Starts the wilderness journey and preserves the route choice, Joseph's bones, and continuing guidance as distinct details.
hotspots.diagram_note: God leads Israel from the Philistine road; Moses carries Joseph’s bones; cloud and fire guide.

intro.title: Exodus 14 · chapter outline
intro.note: This native text diagram separates the chapter into source-based reading stages. Events, instructions, songs, laws, and summaries follow the text; the cards do not claim to depict one place or moment.

hotspots.title: Sea encampment and announced pursuit
hotspots.note: Stage type: instruction and announcement. The LORD directs Israel to encamp by the sea and announces Pharaoh's expected interpretation and pursuit. Keeps the divine instruction and announced outcome upstream of the actual pursuit.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD orders Israel to camp by the sea and foretells Pharaoh’s pursuit.

hotspots.title: Pharaoh's army catches Israel
hotspots.note: Stage type: narrative action. Pharaoh changes course, gathers his chariots and army, and overtakes Israel near the sea. Marks the threat's arrival before Israel's reaction.
hotspots.diagram_note: Pharaoh changes course, gathers his chariots and army, and overtakes Israel near the sea.

hotspots.title: Israel fears; Moses reassures
hotspots.note: Stage type: response and assurance. Israel fears and complains; Moses tells them to stand firm and see the LORD's salvation. Shows the people's crisis and Moses' reassurance as a distinct response beat.
hotspots.diagram_note: Israel fears and complains; Moses tells them to stand firm and see the LORD's salvation.

hotspots.title: The cloud moves between the camps
hotspots.note: Stage type: instruction and protection. The LORD commands Israel to go forward and Moses to stretch out his rod; the angel and cloud move between the camps. Separates command and protective movement from the crossing that follows.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD commands Israel forward; Moses raises his rod as cloud and angel move between camps.

hotspots.title: The sea opens; Israel crosses
hotspots.note: Stage type: action and outcome. The LORD drives back the sea, and Israel enters the midst of it on dry ground between walls of water. Captures the exact painted crossing moment and its textual result.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD drives back the sea, and Israel enters the midst of it on dry ground between walls of water.

hotspots.title: Egypt follows into the sea
hotspots.note: Stage type: action and reported response. Egyptian chariots and horsemen follow into the sea; the LORD troubles them and their chariots drive heavily. Keeps the Egyptian action and their realization separate from the crossing image.
hotspots.diagram_note: Egyptian chariots follow into the sea; the LORD troubles them, and they try to flee.

hotspots.title: The waters return; Israel is saved
hotspots.note: Stage type: command outcome and response. The LORD commands Moses to stretch out his hand; Moses complies, the sea returns and Israel is saved; the people then see the result, fear the LORD, and believe the LORD and Moses. Separates the commanded return of the waters, the narrated outcome, and Israel's response.
hotspots.diagram_note: The waters return, Israel is saved, and the people fear the LORD and believe.

scenes.caption: Editorial chapter diagram · events and instructions are separate reading stages, not one scene

intro.title: Exodus 15 · chapter outline
intro.note: This native text diagram separates the chapter into source-based reading stages. Events, instructions, songs, laws, and summaries follow the text; the cards do not claim to depict one place or moment.

hotspots.title: A song of victory over Egypt
hotspots.note: Stage type: song. Moses and Israel sing of the LORD's victory over Pharaoh's force, power, holiness, and incomparable acts. Preserves the song as poetry and lets the later narrative resume separately.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses and Israel sing of the LORD’s victory, power, holiness, and wonders.

hotspots.title: Guidance and the LORD's reign
hotspots.note: Stage type: song and forward looking claim. The song describes the LORD guiding the redeemed people toward his holy habitation and proclaims his reign. Highlights the song's movement from remembered rescue to anticipated destination and sanctuary.
hotspots.diagram_note: The song describes the LORD guiding the redeemed people toward his holy habitation and proclaims his reign.

hotspots.title: The crossing recalled in prose
hotspots.note: Stage type: narrative summary. The narrator summarizes Pharaoh's force entering the sea, the waters returning, and Israel walking on dry land. Marks the short prose bridge between the song and Miriam's response.
hotspots.diagram_note: The narrator recalls Egypt entering the sea and Israel walking on dry land as waters return.

hotspots.title: Miriam leads the women's song
hotspots.note: Stage type: response song. Miriam leads the women with timbrels and dances and answers with the song's victory refrain. Keeps Miriam's musical response distinct from Moses' longer song and the crossing painting.
hotspots.diagram_note: Miriam leads the women with timbrels and dances and answers with the song's victory refrain.

hotspots.title: Bitter water at Marah
hotspots.note: Stage type: journey crisis action and teaching. After three days without water in Shur, the people reach bitter Marah; Moses cries to the LORD, the water is made sweet, and a statute and teaching follow. Separates the transition, complaint, remedy, and stated test/teaching within one compact episode.
hotspots.diagram_note: At Marah the LORD sweetens bitter water and gives Israel a statute and test.

hotspots.title: Israel camps at Elim
hotspots.note: Stage type: narrative arrival. Israel comes to Elim and encamps by twelve wells of water and seventy palm trees. Gives Elim its own verse-precise stage after the Marah episode.
hotspots.diagram_note: Israel comes to Elim and encamps by twelve wells of water and seventy palm trees.

intro.title: Exodus 16 · chapter outline
intro.note: This native text diagram separates the chapter into source-based reading stages. Events, instructions, songs, laws, and summaries follow the text; the cards do not claim to depict one place or moment.

hotspots.title: Hunger in the wilderness
hotspots.note: Stage type: arrival and complaint. In the wilderness of Sin the congregation murmurs against Moses and Aaron, recalling Egypt's food and fearing hunger. Sets the need before the LORD's announcement of provision.
hotspots.diagram_note: Hungry in the wilderness, Israel complains and longs for Egypt’s food.

hotspots.title: Manna announced, not yet received
hotspots.note: Stage type: instruction and announcement. The LORD announces bread from heaven with daily and sixth-day gathering rules; Moses and Aaron say the people will see the LORD's glory and know who brought them out. Separates promised provision and gathering instructions from the later report of what arrives.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD announces daily bread from heaven and a double portion on the sixth day.

hotspots.title: Quail and measured manna
hotspots.note: Stage type: narrated provision and gathering. Quail covers the camp; after the dew lifts, manna appears and the people gather by the stated measure, with neither excess nor lack. Records the actual provision and equal measure without treating the announcement as fulfillment.
hotspots.diagram_note: Quail arrive; manna appears after the dew, and each gathers a measured share.

hotspots.title: Manna left overnight spoils
hotspots.note: Stage type: instruction and outcome. Moses says not to leave manna until morning; some do, and it spoils, while the daily gathering melts in the sun. Makes the command, disobedient result, and daily limit legible.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses forbids leaving manna overnight; some do, and it spoils.

hotspots.title: Sabbath gathering and rest
hotspots.note: Stage type: instruction response and outcome. A double portion is gathered on the sixth day and kept without spoiling for the Sabbath; some go out on the seventh day and find none, then the people rest. Distinguishes Sabbath instructions from the narrated trial and rest.
hotspots.diagram_note: A double portion is kept for Sabbath; those seeking manna on day seven find none.

hotspots.title: Manna kept as a memorial
hotspots.note: Stage type: memorial instruction and summary. Israel names manna, Moses orders an omer kept before the Testimony for future generations, and the chapter summarizes its long provision and measure. Connects the food episode to a preserved memorial and a long-range summary.
hotspots.diagram_note: Israel names manna; Moses orders an omer kept for future generations.

intro.title: Exodus 17 · chapter outline
intro.note: This native text diagram separates the chapter into source-based reading stages. Events, instructions, songs, laws, and summaries follow the text; the cards do not claim to depict one place or moment.

hotspots.title: Thirst at Rephidim
hotspots.note: Verses 1–3 report thirst and the people’s dispute with Moses; verse 4 records Moses’ cry to the LORD. The question “Is the LORD among us?” comes at 17:7.
hotspots.diagram_note: At Rephidim, Israel lacks water, disputes with Moses, and asks for a drink.

hotspots.title: Water from the rock at Horeb
hotspots.note: Stage type: instruction action and outcome. The LORD tells Moses to take the elders and rod, strike the rock at Horeb, and water comes out; the place is named Massah and Meribah. Keeps the command to Moses, the water outcome, and the naming/explanation together in order.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD tells Moses to strike Horeb’s rock; water flows, and the place is named.

hotspots.title: Joshua fights; Moses is supported
hotspots.note: Stage type: battle sequence and outcome. Amalek fights Israel; Joshua leads fighters while Moses stands on the hill, and Aaron and Hur support his heavy hands until Joshua prevails. Shows the coordinated ground battle and hill actions as a sequence, not a single undifferentiated tableau.
hotspots.diagram_note: Joshua fights Amalek; Aaron and Hur support Moses’s raised hands until Israel prevails.

hotspots.title: Battle memorial and ongoing conflict
hotspots.note: Stage type: memorial command and announcement. The LORD orders a written memorial and instruction to Joshua; Moses builds an altar and names it Jehovah-nissi, followed by the stated ongoing conflict with Amalek. Separates the immediate battle result from its memorial and forward-looking declaration.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses writes a memorial, names an altar Jehovah-nissi, and warns of continuing conflict.

intro.title: Exodus 18 · chapter outline
intro.note: This native text diagram separates the chapter into source-based reading stages. Events, instructions, songs, laws, and summaries follow the text; the cards do not claim to depict one place or moment.

hotspots.title: Jethro arrives with Moses' family
hotspots.note: Stage type: hearing and arrival. Jethro hears what God has done and comes to Moses with Zipporah and the two sons, whose names and explanations are recalled. Establishes the family and arrival before Jethro's response and counsel.
hotspots.diagram_note: Jethro brings Zipporah and Moses’s two sons after hearing what God has done.

hotspots.title: Reunion, report, and shared meal
hotspots.note: Stage type: meeting report and response. Moses welcomes Jethro, reports the deliverance, Jethro rejoices and blesses the LORD, and they share sacrifice and a meal with Aaron and the elders. Shows Jethro's response and shared meal as a distinct episode before the administrative scene.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses reports deliverance; Jethro blesses the LORD and shares a meal with the elders.

hotspots.title: Moses hears cases
hotspots.note: Stage type: observed practice and explanation. Moses sits to judge from morning until evening and explains that he hears disputes and teaches God's statutes and laws. States the practice Jethro observes before presenting his critique.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses judges disputes from morning to evening and teaches God’s statutes.

hotspots.title: Jethro proposes shared judging
hotspots.note: Stage type: critique proposal and conditional benefit. Jethro calls the load unsustainable, advises Moses to teach the people and appoint trustworthy rulers for different-sized groups, and describes the benefit conditionally if God so commands. Keeps counsel as proposal with its stated condition, not as an already completed system.
hotspots.diagram_note: Jethro calls Moses’s load too heavy and advises appointing judges if God commands.

hotspots.title: Moses appoints rulers
hotspots.note: Stage type: implementation and departure. Moses heeds Jethro, appoints rulers, difficult cases come to Moses and smaller cases are judged by them; Jethro departs. Separates the actual implementation from the preceding advice.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses appoints judges; they hear smaller cases, while difficult cases go to him.

intro.title: Exodus 19 · chapter outline
intro.note: This native text diagram separates the chapter into source-based reading stages. Events, instructions, songs, laws, and summaries follow the text; the cards do not claim to depict one place or moment.

hotspots.title: Israel camps before Sinai
hotspots.note: Stage type: arrival. In the third month Israel leaves Rephidim and camps in the wilderness before the mount at Sinai. Sets the place and arrival before the covenant proposal.
hotspots.diagram_note: In the third month Israel leaves Rephidim and camps in the wilderness before the mount at Sinai.

hotspots.title: Covenant proposal and promised identity
hotspots.note: Stage type: announcement and conditional promise. The LORD recalls bringing Israel out and proposes that obedience to his voice and covenant will make them his peculiar treasure, a kingdom of priests, and a holy nation. Makes the covenant condition and promised identity explicit before the people's assent.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD promises Israel a treasured identity if they obey his covenant.

hotspots.title: The people answer; a cloud is announced
hotspots.note: Stage type: response and announcement. Moses relays the words, the people say they will do them, and the LORD announces a thick cloud so they can hear him speak with Moses. Separates Israel's reply from the announced manner of revelation.
hotspots.diagram_note: Israel agrees to the LORD’s words; he announces a thick cloud to speak with Moses.

hotspots.title: Preparation and mountain boundary
hotspots.note: Stage type: instruction and compliance. The LORD orders the people to sanctify themselves and sets limits around the mount; Moses relays the instructions and the people prepare. Keeps the preparation and access restrictions before the third-day event.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD sets Sinai’s boundary and commands Israel to prepare for the third day.

hotspots.title: The LORD descends on Sinai
hotspots.note: Stage type: narrated outcome and summons. On the third day thunder, lightning, cloud, trumpet, smoke, and quaking are narrated; the LORD calls Moses up the mount. Identifies the reported revelation without depicting God or folding in the later warnings.
hotspots.diagram_note: On the third day, thunder, lightning, cloud, trumpet, smoke, and quake; the LORD calls Moses.

hotspots.title: The mountain boundary is reaffirmed
hotspots.note: Stage type: warning instruction and response. The LORD again warns against breaking through the bounds; Moses objects that the limits were already given, and the LORD reiterates who may approach. Keeps the second boundary exchange distinct from the mountain's narrated descent and Moses' summons.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD repeats the Sinai boundary warning; Moses objects, and the LORD restates who may approach.

intro.title: Exodus 20 · chapter outline
intro.note: This native text diagram separates the chapter into source-based reading stages. Events, instructions, songs, laws, and summaries follow the text; the cards do not claim to depict one place or moment.

hotspots.title: Deliverance before the commands
hotspots.note: Stage type: preamble. God identifies himself as the LORD who brought Israel out of Egypt and the house of bondage. Shows the deliverance claim that precedes the commands.
hotspots.diagram_note: God identifies himself as the LORD who brought Israel out of Egypt and the house of bondage.

hotspots.title: Worship, name, and Sabbath commands
hotspots.note: Stage type: command group. Israel is commanded to worship no other gods, make no graven image, honor the LORD's name, and keep the Sabbath, with the Sabbath grounded in creation. Groups the opening commands while retaining their distinct topics and stated Sabbath rationale.
hotspots.diagram_note: Israel must reject other gods and images, honor the LORD’s name, and keep Sabbath.

hotspots.title: Commands toward family and neighbor
hotspots.note: Stage type: command group. The commands address honoring parents and prohibit killing, adultery, theft, false witness, and coveting. Makes the shift to family and neighbor-facing commands easy to scan.
hotspots.diagram_note: Commands honor parents; they forbid killing, adultery, theft, false witness, and coveting.

hotspots.title: The people ask Moses to mediate
hotspots.note: Stage type: response and mediation. The people see and hear the mountain's signs, stand afar off, ask Moses to speak instead, and Moses tells them not to fear but not to sin. Separates the people's response from the commands that follow.
hotspots.diagram_note: The people ask Moses to speak instead; he says not to fear but not to sin.

hotspots.title: No gods of silver or gold
hotspots.note: Stage type: instruction. The LORD says Israel has heard him from heaven and must make no silver or gold gods alongside him. Keeps the direct anti-idol instruction separate from altar construction.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD says Israel has heard him from heaven and must make no silver or gold gods alongside him.

hotspots.title: Instructions for the altar
hotspots.note: Stage type: instruction. The LORD instructs Israel to make an earth altar, or an unhewn-stone altar, with no steps, and states where he will meet and bless them. Shows the altar rules and their stated promise as a compact closing unit.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD commands an earth or unhewn-stone altar with no steps and promises to meet Israel.

hotspots.title: Household service and release rules
hotspots.note: Stage type: law group. Judgments cover Hebrew servants, release and chosen continued service, and rules concerning a daughter sold as a maidservant and her treatment. Groups the chapter's opening household-status rules without turning them into narrative events.
hotspots.diagram_note: Rules cover Hebrew servants, release, chosen service, and daughters sold as maidservants.

hotspots.title: Life and family offenses
hotspots.note: Stage type: law group. Judgments distinguish killing from unplanned harm and address striking or cursing parents and stealing a person for sale. Keeps these serious offenses together while preserving the text's distinctions.
hotspots.diagram_note: Judgments address killing, striking or cursing parents, and kidnapping for sale.

hotspots.title: Injury and compensation
hotspots.note: Stage type: law group. Cases address injury in a fight, harm to a pregnant woman, proportional penalties, and injury to a servant's eye or tooth with release provisions. Makes the range of injury cases and compensation rules visible in one legal unit.
hotspots.diagram_note: Cases cover fighting injuries, harm to a pregnant woman, penalties, and servant release.

hotspots.title: Animals and pit liability
hotspots.note: Stage type: law group. Judgments address a goring ox, known danger and owner responsibility, ransom and servant compensation, uncovered pits, and ox-on-ox injury. Highlights liability according to known risk and the separate pit and animal cases.
hotspots.diagram_note: The law addresses goring oxen, known danger, pits, ransom, and ox-on-ox injury.

hotspots.title: Theft and property damage
hotspots.note: Stage type: law group. Restitution rules address stolen livestock, a thief, grazing another's field, and damage caused by fire. Groups direct property taking with neighboring cases of property damage.
hotspots.diagram_note: Restitution rules address stolen livestock, a thief, grazing another's field, and damage caused by fire.

hotspots.title: Entrusted or borrowed property
hotspots.note: Stage type: law group. Rules address entrusted money and goods, disputes before judges, animals kept for another, theft or injury, and borrowed or hired property. Separates custody and borrowing responsibilities from theft and damage rules.
hotspots.diagram_note: Rules address entrusted goods, disputes, animals kept for others, and borrowed property.

hotspots.title: Obligation after enticement
hotspots.note: Stage type: law group. A man who entices an unbetrothed maid must endow her as his wife; if her father refuses, he still pays the stated money. Preserves this specific obligation as its own provision.
hotspots.diagram_note: The man must provide a dowry; if her father refuses marriage, he still pays.

hotspots.title: Forbidden practices
hotspots.note: Stage type: prohibition group. The text prohibits sorcery, sex with an animal, and sacrifice to another god. Makes the three short prohibitions easy to find without conflating them with social protections.
hotspots.diagram_note: The text prohibits sorcery, sex with an animal, and sacrifice to another god.

hotspots.title: Protect strangers and vulnerable neighbors
hotspots.note: Stage type: law and rationale. Israel must not oppress a stranger, widow, or fatherless child; rules protect poor borrowers and require returning a neighbor's pledged garment by sundown. Connects the protections to Israel's own strangerhood and the stated divine response.
hotspots.diagram_note: The law protects strangers, widows, orphans, poor borrowers, and pledged garments.

hotspots.title: First gifts and holy conduct
hotspots.note: Stage type: instruction group. The text commands reverence, timely first offerings and firstborn, and holy conduct concerning flesh torn by beasts. Gathers the chapter's closing obligations while distinguishing them from case law.
hotspots.diagram_note: Israel must honor God, give first produce and firstborn, and reject flesh torn by beasts.

hotspots.title: Justice, testimony, and neighbor help
hotspots.note: Stage type: law group and rationale. Commands reject false reports, majority-driven wrongdoing, partial judgment, and gifts that distort justice; they require helping an enemy's animal and not oppressing a stranger. Collects courtroom integrity with practical fairness toward enemies and strangers.
hotspots.diagram_note: The law forbids false witness and partial judgment, aiding enemies’ animals and strangers.

hotspots.title: Seventh-year and weekly rest
hotspots.note: Stage type: calendar instruction. The land rests in the seventh year for the poor and beasts; weekly rest refreshes workers, animals, and the stranger, alongside a warning about other gods. Shows recurring rest rules and their stated beneficiaries.
hotspots.diagram_note: The land rests in year seven; weekly rest refreshes workers, animals, and strangers.

hotspots.title: Annual feasts and offerings
hotspots.note: Stage type: festival and offering instruction. Three annual feasts are named, with instructions about unleavened bread, harvest, ingathering, and offerings of blood, fat, and firstfruits. Makes the festival cycle and associated offering rules readable as one calendar unit.
hotspots.diagram_note: Three yearly feasts mark unleavened bread, harvest, and ingathering, with offering rules.

hotspots.title: Messenger and conditional promise
hotspots.note: Stage type: announcement warning and conditional promise. The LORD announces an Angel to lead Israel, warns them to obey, and promises opposition to their enemies if they obey. Keeps the messenger's announced role and obedience condition distinct from later land-outcome promises.
hotspots.diagram_note: An Angel leads Israel; the LORD commands obedience and promises aid against enemies.

hotspots.title: Worship and promised blessing
hotspots.note: Stage type: instruction and promise. Israel must not serve the nations' gods but must serve the LORD, who promises blessing for bread and water and fertility and long life. Shows the prohibition, positive instruction, and promised result together.
hotspots.diagram_note: Israel must serve the LORD, who promises food, water, fertility, and long life.

hotspots.title: Future land and boundaries
hotspots.note: Stage type: announcement and promise. The LORD announces fear, hornets, and a gradual driving out of inhabitants, and states the land's boundaries and Israel's role. Separates announced future outcomes and boundaries from the preceding worship commands.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD promises fear, hornets, gradual removal of peoples, and land boundaries.

hotspots.title: No covenant with local gods
hotspots.note: Stage type: prohibition and warning. Israel must make no covenant with the inhabitants or their gods; their presence and worship are warned to become a snare. Ends the chapter on its explicit covenant prohibition and stated risk.
hotspots.diagram_note: Israel must make no covenant with local peoples or gods, lest worship become a snare.

hotspots.title: Instructions for approaching
hotspots.note: Stage type: instruction. Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders are told to worship afar off; Moses alone may come near. Sets roles and access limits before the covenant words are read and enacted.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders are told to worship afar off; Moses alone may come near.

hotspots.title: The covenant is read and ratified
hotspots.note: Stage type: narrative ceremony and response. Moses reports and writes the words, builds an altar and twelve pillars, offerings are made, the covenant book is read, the people assent, and Moses applies blood while naming the covenant. Preserves the ceremony's order and separates the people's assent from the blood rite.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses reads the covenant; the people assent, offerings are made, and blood seals it.

hotspots.title: The elders see and eat
hotspots.note: Stage type: narrated encounter and meal. Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders go up, see the described pavement beneath the God of Israel, and eat and drink; no harm comes to them. Keeps this distinct encounter and meal separate from the public covenant rite and Moses' later ascent.
hotspots.diagram_note: The elders see God of Israel and sapphire-like pavement, then eat and drink unharmed.

hotspots.title: Moses enters the cloud
hotspots.note: Stage type: instruction ascent and duration. The LORD calls Moses for stone tablets and law; Moses leaves Joshua with him, the cloud covers the mount, and Moses enters it for forty days and nights. Separates the instruction to ascend from the narrated cloud, glory, and duration.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses enters the cloud on Sinai and remains forty days and nights.

hotspots.title: Moses asks for the LORD’s presence
hotspots.note: Moses asks to know the LORD’s way and for his presence to go with Israel; the LORD says his presence will go.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses asks the LORD’s presence to go with Israel, and the LORD agrees.

hotspots.title: Moses asks for glory; passing is guarded
hotspots.note: Moses asks to see the LORD’s glory; the LORD hides him in a cleft of rock and shields him as the glory passes.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses asks to see glory; the LORD shields him in a cleft of rock.

hotspots.title: New tablets and the LORD’s proclamation
hotspots.note: Verses 1–9 narrate Moses’ ascent with new tablets, the LORD’s proclamation, and Moses’ plea; covenant terms follow from verse 10.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses brings new tablets; the LORD proclaims his name and Moses pleads for Israel.

hotspots.title: Covenant promises and warnings against other gods
hotspots.note: Verses 10–17 give covenant promises and warn Israel against other gods, images, and covenants with the inhabitants.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD renews the covenant and warns Israel against other gods.

hotspots.title: Feasts, firstborn, Sabbath, and offerings
hotspots.note: Verses 18–26 give feast, firstborn, Sabbath, offering, and firstfruits instructions.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD gives feast, firstborn, Sabbath, and offering instructions.

hotspots.title: Covenant words and forty days and nights
hotspots.note: Verses 27–28 command Moses to write the covenant words and report his forty days and nights on Sinai.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses writes the covenant words after forty days and nights on Sinai.

hotspots.title: Moses returns with a shining face and uses a veil
hotspots.note: Verses 29–35 report Moses’ shining face, Israel’s fear, his words, and the veil he uses when not before the LORD.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses returns with a shining face and uses a veil when not before the LORD.

hotspots.title: Sabbath rest repeated before the work instructions
hotspots.note: Moses commands six days of work and seventh-day rest, and forbids kindling fire in Israel’s dwellings on Sabbath.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses commands Sabbath rest and forbids kindling fire on that day.

hotspots.title: Materials and work to be made
hotspots.note: Moses calls for willing gifts and lists materials, furnishings, and sanctuary work.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses lists willing gifts and the sanctuary furnishings to be made.

hotspots.title: Willing gifts, spinning, stones, and spices
hotspots.note: The people bring willing offerings; women spin goats’ hair, and rulers bring stones, spices, and oil.
hotspots.diagram_note: The people bring offerings; women spin thread, and rulers bring stones and spices.

hotspots.title: Bezalel and Aholiab lead skilled work
hotspots.note: Moses names Bezalel and Aholiab to lead and teach the skilled work.
hotspots.diagram_note: Bezalel and Aholiab are appointed to lead and teach skilled work.

hotspots.title: Work begins; further giving is stopped
hotspots.note: Craftsmen begin work; the people bring more than enough, so Moses tells them to stop giving.
hotspots.diagram_note: Craftsmen begin work; offerings exceed need, so Moses stops further giving.

hotspots.title: Curtains, loops, clasps, and coverings
hotspots.note: Workers make the linen curtains, loops and clasps, goats’ hair curtains, and outer coverings; the text gives no stitching pattern.
hotspots.diagram_note: Workers make coupled linen and goats’ hair curtains and outer coverings.

hotspots.title: Boards, supports, bars, and gold overlay
hotspots.note: Verses 20–34 report making boards, sockets, corner supports, bars, and gold overlay. The text gives dimensions and features; this is not a complete measured construction plan.
hotspots.diagram_note: Workers make the boards, sockets, corner supports, bars, and gold overlay.

hotspots.title: Inner veil and entrance hanging are made
hotspots.note: Workers make the inner veil and the separate entrance hanging.
hotspots.diagram_note: Workers make the inner veil and the tent entrance hanging.

hotspots.title: Table, border, rings, poles, and vessels are made

hotspots.diagram_note: The table, border, rings, poles, and gold vessels are made.

detail.alt: Illustration of the gold-covered table holding the shewbread

hotspots.title: Lampstand, branches, lamps, and utensils are made

hotspots.diagram_note: The beaten-gold lampstand, branches, lamps, and utensils are made.

detail.alt: Illustration of the golden seven-branched candlestick and its lamps

hotspots.title: Incense altar, oil, and incense are made

hotspots.title: Bronze laver and foot are made
hotspots.note: Verse 8 says the laver and base are made from the mirrors of women assembled at the tent entrance; the basin art is a reconstruction.

hotspots.title: Court hangings, pillars, gate, and pins are made

hotspots.diagram_note: Workers make the court hangings, pillars, gate screen, cords, and pins.

hotspots.title: Tabernacle inventory and named craftsmen
hotspots.note: Verses 21–23 give the inventory and name Ithamar, Bezalel, and Aholiab.
hotspots.diagram_note: The inventory names Ithamar, Bezalel, and Aholiab as overseers and craftsmen.

hotspots.title: Gold, silver, and brass totals and their uses
hotspots.note: Verses 24–31 account for gold, silver, and brass and specify uses; take quantities from the text, not an illustration.
hotspots.diagram_note: The account totals gold, silver, and brass and lists uses of some materials.

hotspots.title: Ephod and shoulder stones are made
hotspots.note: Verses 1–7 report making the ephod, girdle, and shoulder stones engraved with Israel’s names.
hotspots.diagram_note: Workers make the ephod, its girdle, and shoulder stones engraved with Israel’s names.

hotspots.title: Breastplate and fastening are made
hotspots.note: Verses 8–21 report making the breastplate, its named stones and fastenings, and attaching it to the ephod.
hotspots.diagram_note: The breastplate’s stones, tribal names, chains, rings, and fastening are made.

hotspots.title: Blue robe, pomegranates, and bells are made
hotspots.note: Verses 22–26 report making the blue robe with alternating golden bells and pomegranates.
hotspots.diagram_note: The blue robe is made with alternating golden bells and pomegranates.

hotspots.title: Coats, headwear, girdle, and gold plate
hotspots.note: Verses 27–31 report making coats, headwear, girdles, linen breeches, and the gold plate engraved “HOLINESS TO THE LORD.”
hotspots.diagram_note: Coats, headwear, girdles, linen breeches, and a gold plate are made.

hotspots.title: Finished work is inspected and blessed
hotspots.note: Verses 32–43 report the finished work brought to Moses, his inspection, and his blessing of the people.
hotspots.diagram_note: The finished work is brought to Moses, inspected, found as commanded, and blessed.

hotspots.title: Commanded setup and furniture placement
hotspots.note: Verses 1–15 command the setup; verses 16–33 report Moses carrying it out.
hotspots.diagram_note: The LORD tells Moses to place the ark, table, lamp, altars, laver, and court.

hotspots.title: Anointing, sanctification, and priestly clothing
hotspots.note: Verses 9–15 instruct Moses to anoint the sanctuary and furnishings and consecrate Aaron and his sons.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses is told to anoint the Tabernacle and furnishings and consecrate Aaron and his sons.

hotspots.title: Moses assembles the court and furnishings
hotspots.note: Verses 16–33 report Moses completing the commanded setup, washing Aaron and his sons, and finishing the court.
hotspots.diagram_note: Moses erects and furnishes the Tabernacle, washes the priests, and completes the court.

hotspots.title: Cloud fills Tabernacle; cloud and fire guide
hotspots.note: Verses 34–38 report the cloud filling the tent, Moses unable to enter, and Israel traveling by the cloud/fire signal. The existing overview is a still reconstruction, not a narrative depiction of this event.
hotspots.diagram_note: The cloud fills the tent; Israel travels when it lifts, with cloud by day and fire by night.
